new_jobs.title: Project Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Project Coordinator

**Company:** Componentry  
**Location:** Fremont, CA — fully onsite  
**Reports to:** President  
**Type:** Full-time, non-exempt, hourly  
**Schedule:** Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m., including a 30-minute unpaid meal break  
**Pay:** $28–$42 per hour, depending on relevant experience and demonstrated skills

About Componentry

Componentry helps hardware companies source and manage materials, build electronic and electromechanical assemblies, and keep production moving. We work as an extension of our customers’ teams, from quoting and procurement through production.

We’re looking for a Project Coordinator to connect the people, information, and actions needed to carry customer jobs from order review through delivery.

The role

You’ll maintain a clear picture of active jobs, follow up on commitments, identify risks, and coordinate solutions so work keeps moving.

Working directly with our President, you’ll partner with procurement, receiving, production, suppliers, and customers. You’ll track what has been purchased, what is outstanding, what is ready to kit or build, and what needs to happen to meet delivery commitments.

You’ll own the shared job dashboard and connect existing purchasing sheets, receiving records, and production schedules. Information should be accessible to the team without someone having to reconstruct a status report whenever an update is needed.

We’re open to training someone with strong organization, initiative, and follow-through. Your independence and decision-making authority will grow as you learn our business and demonstrate sound judgment.

What you’ll ownJob planning and visibility

* Review new orders against quoted lead times, checking material availability and production capacity with the team.
* Establish job milestones and flag conditions that could affect the expected schedule.
* Maintain the shared job dashboard, including purchasing progress, material delivery dates, receiving status, kit readiness, production, inspection, and shipment.
* Connect information across existing records and improve trackers and handoffs where needed.
* Keep blockers, next actions, owners, and deadlines visible.
* Establish regular updates with the team and escalate missing information or unresolved actions that put delivery at risk.
* Maintain traceability between customer jobs, purchase orders, and materials, including purchases supporting multiple jobs.

Follow-through and recovery

* Follow up with procurement on unpurchased items, supplier commitments, outstanding deliveries, and purchasing blockers.
* Follow up with receiving and production on discrepancies, kit completion, build progress, inspection, and rework.
* Identify stalled work, establish the next action with the responsible person, and follow through to resolution.
* Develop recovery plans with procurement and production, using their expertise to evaluate feasible options.
* Coordinate recovery actions and authorize expenses within established limits as responsibility grows.
* Escalate competing customer priorities, unresolved feasibility disagreements, and decisions outside your authority with options and a recommendation.
* Raise risks early enough for the team to respond.

Customer and supplier communication

* Confirm customer requirements, requested dates, and delivery arrangements.
* Obtain supplier shipment commitments, tracking information, and missing documents.
* Communicate job progress, outstanding dependencies, and schedule changes clearly.
* Work with the team and customer to agree on achievable recovery dates within established authority.
* Document commitments and confirm completion through customer delivery.
* Keep the President informed through frequent, concise updates and priority discussions.
* Clearly hand off unresolved issues requiring attention after your workday ends.

Project-related support

* Assist with sourcing, purchasing follow-ups, and documentation needed to move assigned jobs forward.
* Coordinate resolution of supplier account or administrative issues affecting project schedules.
* Take on other defined projects as agreed with the President, with priorities adjusted to match available capacity.

How responsibilities fit together

Procurement owns purchasing records and supplier purchasing activity. Receiving owns receiving records and material discrepancies. Production owns its schedule and execution.

You own the integrated job dashboard, cross-team follow-through, and coordination through customer delivery. You’ll work with these team members to identify risks, evaluate their recommendations, and drive next steps.

You’ll have the President’s backing to request timely updates, establish action deadlines with the team, and escalate unresolved commitments. Functional leads remain accountable for execution within their areas.

The President resolves competing customer priorities, significant escalations, and decisions beyond your authority. Customer delivery takes priority over additional internal projects.

What we’re looking for

* Evidence of taking responsibility and seeing work through completion.
* Strong organization across multiple tasks, deadlines, and changing priorities.
* Resourcefulness when information is missing or instructions are incomplete.
* Willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback, and apply what you learn.
* Confidence following up with experienced teammates, suppliers, and customers.
* Clear written and verbal communication.
* Attention to detail with dates, quantities, part numbers, documents, and records.
* Judgment about when to act, when to seek input, and when to escalate.
* Comfort working with spreadsheets, shared trackers, email, and business software.
* A collaborative approach and dependable follow-through without repeated reminders.

Relevant experience may come from project coordination, administration, purchasing, logistics, retail, hospitality, or other responsibilities requiring organization and owne

The Research Program Coordinator will serve as a key analyst and coordinator supporting the programmatic and research activities of the Principal Investigator within UCSF’s Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology & Reproductive Sciences.

The position supports multiple grant-funded research projects focused on patient-provider communication, particularly in the areas of pharmacies, sexual and reproductive health, and empathy in healthcare. The Coordinator will conduct moderately complex qualitative and quantitative analytical work, support manuscript preparation and submission, and coordinate research, teaching, and mentorship activities. The Coordinator will collaborate with UCSF departments, the San Francisco Department of Public Health, research and administrative partners, and outside consultants. The role will also evaluate research processes, data collection and storage practices, and available technologies and services to identify alternatives and make sound recommendations.

The role is based within the department’s Zuckerberg San Francisco General division, whose mission includes promoting justice, quality, and equity in women’s healthcare.

new_jobs.title: Executive Assistant & Business Partner to the CEO
new_jobs.description:
**Executive Assistant & Business Partner to the CEO — (San Francisco, CA)**

**Full-time | In-person | 5+ years of relevant experience required**

**FurtherAI** is building the AI Workspace for Insurance, empowering underwriters, brokers, and carriers to automate routine work so they can focus on higher-value decisions. We move fast, prioritize clarity and quality, and value effective, high-integrity work.

**The role**
------------

This is not a traditional EA job. You'll be the CEO's right hand: part Executive Assistant, part Executive Business Partner, and the owner of how it feels to work at FurtherAI day to day.

You'll own the CEO's time, priorities, and follow-through end to end, so the most important work keeps moving and nothing falls between conversations. You'll also build the workplace experience from the ground up: our office, our rituals, our offsites, and the small details that make a fast-growing team feel like a team.

The best person for this role acts as a force multiplier. You anticipate needs before they're voiced, reduce the CEO's cognitive load, and bring the judgment to decide what deserves attention and what doesn't. As we scale, this role grows with you.

**What you'll do**
------------------

### **Run the CEO's time and attention**

* Own the CEO's calendar end to end: sequence priorities, protect focus time, anticipate conflicts, and decide what truly needs their time.
* Triage the CEO's inbox, surface what matters, and draft clear, thoughtful replies on their behalf.
* Coordinate complex scheduling across customers, investors, candidates, press, and the internal team.
* Plan travel and logistics end to end, with the right prep and follow-through built in.
* Handle occasional personal logistics (appointments, vendors, travel) with discretion and sound judgment.

### **Be a true business partner**

* Make sure the CEO walks into every key meeting prepared: agendas, pre-reads, context, and who's in the room.
* Capture decisions and action items, then drive follow-through so nothing important gets lost.
* Build and run a lightweight operating system for priorities, open loops, and commitments.
* Own logistics and prep for board meetings, investor updates, and leadership syncs.
* Take on special projects with the CEO and leadership team: research, process improvements, and cross-functional initiatives.

### **Own the workplace experience**

* Run the San Francisco office: space, vendors, supplies, food, and making sure it works for the team every day.
* Plan team offsites, all-hands, celebrations, and customer or candidate events.
* Partner with Recruiting and People on onboarding, so every new hire feels welcome and productive from day one.
* Shape and scale our culture through rituals, engagement initiatives, and internal communications.
* Build the processes and documentation that help the office and team run smoothly as we grow across locations.

**What success looks like**
---------------------------

* **First 30 days:** You know the CEO's priorities, working style, and key relationships. Their calendar and inbox run smoothly, and you've got a handle on how the office runs today.
* **First 90 days:** You're trusted to make calls on the CEO's behalf. You've built the operating rhythm for meeting prep and follow-through, and you've run your first offsite or company event.
* **First year:** The CEO spends more of their time on the highest-impact work because of you. The workplace experience is something candidates notice and the team is proud of.

**About you**
-------------

* 5 to 8+ years supporting a founder, CEO, or C-suite leader, ideally at a fast-growing startup.
* Experience owning office or workplace operations, events, or team culture programs.
* Excellent judgment and discretion, with a track record of handling confidential information.
* Highly organized and detail-oriented without losing speed. You build structure where there is none.
* A clear, warm communicator who adapts to different styles and builds trust across every team.
* You anticipate needs, spot issues early, and fix them without being asked.
* Calm and effective in a high-stakes, fast-changing environment.
* Fluent in modern tools: Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, and AI assistants like Claude or ChatGPT.
* Based in San Francisco and excited to be in the office 5 days a week.
* Bonus: experience at an AI or B2B SaaS company.

### **This role is not for you if**

* You prefer a rigid, predictable, or slow-moving environment.
* You want to manage rather than roll up your sleeves and do.
* You're not excited about high ownership and hands-on execution.
* You can't work in person in San Francisco.
* Work/life balance is important to you

**Why Join FurtherAI:**

* Partner closely with founders/leadership at a fast-growing AI company
* Gain exposure and responsibility across all aspects of early-stage operations
* Help shape culture and foundational processes
* Receive competitive salary, equity, and benefits
* Join a team that values speed, communication, and craftsmanship

**You can look forward to the following benefits:**

* Fully covered, best-in-class health, dental, and vision benefits
* Competitive Compensation, meaningful stock options, company 401(k)
* Unlimited PTO
* Outstanding in-office culture in the heart of San Francisco
* Lunch and dinner onsite
* Team events, such as happy hours and off-sites
* Commuter benefits

Compensation Range: $140K - $165K

We are seeking a highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented Business Development Representative (BDR) to support MediaGo's sales and business development team. This role will focus on researching advertisers, agencies, market opportunities, and industry trends while helping the team maintain accurate reporting, prospect records, CRM data, and business development documentation.

This role requires strong communication, excellent cross-functional team collaboration, and the ability to support multiple team members in a fast-moving environment. Professional Mandarin skills are required for communication with Mandarin-speaking partners and internal stakeholders.

This position is ideal for someone who is highly organized, reliable, curious, and eager to develop practical experience in digital advertising, sales operations, market research, and business development.

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Prospect and Market Research: Research potential advertisers, agencies, decision-makers, industries, competitors, market trends, and business opportunities to support MediaGo's sales efforts.

**Qualifications:**

* Experience in business development, sales operations, market research, reporting, data management, administrative support, or a related field is preferred.

* Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy when working with data, CRM systems, spreadsheets, and documentation.

* Excellent cross-functional team communication and the ability to work effectively with Sales, Account Management, Operations, and other teams.
* Excellent Mandarin skills are required, including the ability to communicate professionally with Mandarin-speaking partners and stakeholders.

**Culture Fit:**

* Detail-oriented: You take ownership of accuracy and understand the importance of reliable records, reporting, and documentation.
* Research-driven: You enjoy finding information, identifying patterns, and turning research into useful insights for the team.
* Self-directed: You can manage priorities, follow through on assignments, and work independently with limited supervision.
* Team-oriented: You communicate clearly, support your colleagues, and contribute to shared goals across departments.
* Adaptable: You are comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities and assignments may change.

Who We Are
  
The Fund for Public Health in New York City (FPHNYC) is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that is dedicated to the advancement of the health and well-being of all New Yorkers. To this end, in partnership with the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH), FPHNYC incubates innovative public health initiatives implemented by DOHMH to advance community health throughout the city. It facilitates partnerships, often new and unconventional, between government and the private sector to develop, test, and launch new initiatives. These collaborations speed the execution of demonstration projects, effect expansion of successful pilot programs, and support rapid implementation to meet the public health needs of individuals, families, and communities across New York City.
  
  
Our Culture
  
We embrace a culture of learning, collaboration, innovation, and well-being, where open communication drives our impact.
  
About The Role
  
The Program Coordinator will support the day-to-day implementation of the Nest and Nourish program, a HRSA-funded prescription produce program for pregnant and postpartum individuals. The position will serve as a primary point of contact for participants, including coordinating enrollment, navigation, referrals, follow-up, data collection, and retention activities. The coordinator will work closely with clinical partners, community-based organizations, program staff, and program leadership to ensure effective implementation of the program.
  
About the Program
  
Nest & Nourish is a program of the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene’s Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health that aims to improve maternal health by increasing food access and security among pregnant and postpartum participants. The program provides produce benefits, nutrition education, case management, and connections to community resources. This program is one of several food access initiatives in the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health.

* Coordinate participant recruitment, eligibility screening, enrollment, and orientation to services.
* Serve as a primary point of contact for participants during program engagement.
* Conduct regular participants check-ins and assess food access, social needs, and barriers to participation.
* Coordinate distribution and tracking of monthly benefits.
* Monitor participant engagement, voucher redemption, nutrition education participation, and retention. Provide referrals and navigation assistance to other bureau programs and community resource activities.
* Coordinate required nutrition education classes, cooking demonstrations, and other program activities.
* Conduct reminder and re-engagement outreach for participants who miss appointments or program activities.
* Maintain accurate and timely participant records in accordance with program and privacy requirements.
* Collect survey data and other program evaluation data and support monitoring of data quality.
* Support program outreach, community engagement, and recruitment events.
* Prepare routine program updates and identify participants’ needs, barriers, and opportunities for improvement.
* Support grant deliverables, reporting, and program implantation activities.

Requirements
  

* A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and two years of experience in community work or community centered activities in an area related to the duties described above; or
* High school graduation or equivalent and six years of experience in community work or community centered activities in an area related to the duties as described above; or
* Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. However, all candidates must have at least one year of experience as described in "1" above.
* Strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through.
* Excellent organizational skills and highly detailed oriented
* Excellent oral and written communication skills
* Demonstrated ability to effectively establish and maintain working relationships with culturally diverse community groups.
* Bilingual (written and spoken) Spanish language proficiency preferred.

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check

* A retirement savings plan with generous employer contribution

new_jobs.title: Customer Success Representative
new_jobs.description:
**Who We Are**  
Porter Logistics started in 2017 with two founders, one 3,000-square-foot warehouse and no customers. We won our first accounts one at a time by taking on the work other warehouses turned down and doing the work better than our clients expected.  
  
Today Porter runs four facilities across Atlanta and the Savannah port area. We handle the hard stuff: hazardous and specialty chemicals, food-grade and temperature-controlled freight from ambient to frozen, bonded imports and bulk chemical repackaging. Our customers include Fortune 500 manufacturers and global distributors in chemicals, food and beverage, consumer goods and building materials. They have their pick of 3PLs. They choose us.  
  
We've grown every year since we opened, and 2026 is on pace for 40% growth. Growth means new sites, new roles and room to move up. Many of our leaders started in entry-level roles here.  
  
**The Role**  
As a Customer Sucecss Representative, you'll be the first call for our clients and the source of clean, accurate orders for our warehouse team. Each day you'll enter client orders into our WMS, build pick lists and shipping documents, update the warehouse team on changes and priorities, close completed orders and bill each shipment. When an order, inventory count or shipment goes wrong, you'll track down the cause and work with the warehouse to fix the problem.  
  
This is a full-time hourly position based on-site at our Atlanta warehouse.  
  
**What You'll Earn**

* 20-22/hour based on experience
* Medical, dental and vision plans
* 401(k)
* Paid time off and company holidays
* Occasional overtime opportunities

**Schedule**

* Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM

  
**You'll Thrive Here If You**

* Catch a wrong SKU or quantity before an order reaches the floor
* Like owning a short list of clients and knowing every detail of their accounts
* Stay calm and clear when a client calls about a late shipment
* Want to grow with a company adding new sites and new clients

  
**This Might Not Be For You If**

* You prefer one task at a time. You'll manage orders for 3 to 5 clients at once.
* You'd rather pass a problem along than own the fix
* You want a role with no accountability for billing errors

  
**What You'll Be Responsible For**

* Serve as the main point of contact for 3 to 5 client accounts.
* Enter daily client orders into the WMS accurately.
* Share order details, changes and priorities with the warehouse team.
* Generate pick lists, order packets and outbound shipping documents.
* Investigate and resolve order, inventory and fulfillment issues.
* Close out completed orders in the WMS.
* Bill shipments to the correct client accounts.

  
**What We're Looking For**

* 1+ year in customer service, operations support or a similar role requiring strong attention to detail, organization and customer service skills
* Clear, professional phone and email communication
* Strong organization across several accounts at once
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Outlook and Word
* WMS experience preferred, not required
* Logistics, warehousing or supply chain experience preferred, not required

  
**The Hiring Process**  
We respect your time. If your background fits, a member of our HR team will call you for a short phone screen. Next, you'll visit the warehouse for an in-person interview, meet the team and tour the facility.

new_jobs.title: Business Development Representative (BDR)
new_jobs.description:
**About Climb**
===============

Climb is an AI-native Data & AI consultancy and Databricks partner. We help healthcare, life sciences, financial services and insurance companies get data and AI projects out of pilot and into production. Instead of large consulting teams, we staff small, senior engineering pods on fixed-scope engagements that reach production in 8 to 12 weeks.

We build long-term partnerships with the data teams we work with, and we grow our people the same way: through direct mentorship from founders and senior architects and real exposure to enterprise deals from day one.

**Role Summary**
================

We're looking for a Business Development Representative to open new accounts for Climb across regulated industries. You'll research companies running on Databricks or evaluating it, find the business problems their data teams are stuck on, and start conversations with the people who own them. You'll pair directly with a senior member of Climb’s GTM team and work alongside our solution architects and Databricks account teams on every pursuit, and you'll see how enterprise consulting deals are scoped and won.

We don't have a big-brand inbound engine. Every meeting we book comes from someone who found the right account, figured out who owned the problem, and started a real conversation.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

* Drive new-logo acquisition across healthcare, life sciences, financial services and insurance accounts.
* Build and manage pipeline through outbound prospecting across phone, email and LinkedIn, plus referrals and industry events.
* Plan and run account-based campaigns into named target accounts, coordinated with marketing and your Databricks counterparts.
* Build relationships across data, IT, compliance and executive leadership, and understand who decides what.
* Identify business challenges and translate them into data, analytics and AI opportunities our architects can scope.
* Run discovery on early-stage opportunities and co-run deals alongside your sales partner.
* Co-sell with Databricks account teams on shared accounts in your territory, and run a recurring sync with your assigned Databricks account executives and partner managers.
* Collaborate with solution architects and delivery leads to shape winning pursuits.
* Travel to represent Climb at client meetings, Databricks events, industry forums and Climb-hosted workshops.
* Track your activity and results, and help shape the playbook as we grow.

**What Success Looks Like**
===========================

* **30 days:** You know our offerings and target accounts, and you've met your Databricks counterparts and set a recurring sync with each.
* **60 days:** You're booking qualified meetings you sourced yourself every week.
* **90 days:** You're consistently hitting your pipeline target and have contributed to at least one active opportunity.
* **6 months:** You're at full pipeline target, running discovery on your own, and co-running opportunities with your GTM partner.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

* 2+ years in a BDR or SDR seat, with a track record of meetings you sourced yourself, not just inbound follow-up.
* Experience selling to technical, IT or data buyers. Backgrounds in data infrastructure, cloud, developer tools or technical recruiting are a strong fit.
* Comfort with cold calling and hunting for contacts, and the ability to explain why you went after an account and why you started with the person you did.
* Ability to research accounts and understand buyer personas and decision-making structures.
* Curiosity about how data platforms and AI work, and the drive to learn the technology well enough to discuss it with an engineer.
* Strong client-facing presence and clear, concise writing.
* Bonus: Experience in or selling into healthcare, life sciences, financial services or insurance.

**Who Thrives Here**
====================

This role is designed for BDRs who build their own pipeline today and are growing toward owning accounts and closing deals.

* You'd rather build your own target list than wait for inbound leads.
* You know why you're calling an account, and who owns the problem, before you pick up the phone.
* You're curious about how data and AI work, and you're not shy about asking an engineer to explain it.
* You take rejection in stride and make the next call just as sharp.

**Why Climb**
=============

* **Learn from the builders.** Work directly with founders and senior architects from your first week.
* **Room to grow.** A clear path to Account Executive, with a promotion review at 12 months tied to sourced pipeline and conversion.
* **Where enterprise AI happens.** A front-row view of the Databricks ecosystem and enterprise AI work.
* **Ground floor opportunity.** Join early alongside seasoned founders to help construct our growth playbook from day one.
* **Focus on outcomes.** We measure success by tangible business value and account expansion rather than arbitrary utilization metrics.
* **Senior engineering pods.** Work directly with elite technical teams and AI tooling, free from management bloat.

$26hr for 15-20 hours a week for 40 weeks

Job Duties and Responsibilities

**General Job Description**

The MCMF Mentor Coach is primarily responsible for providing mentorship, guidance, coaching, and direct support to youth ages 16–24 employed through the My CHI My Future Program in partnership with the Chicago Department of Family and Support Services (DFSS).

The Mentor Coach will provide direct services to a caseload of 15 youth over a pre-scheduled 40-week program period, with a required commitment of 800 hours annually, in accordance with the funder-approved program schedule. This position is responsible for supporting youth employment, professional development, participant engagement, payroll administration, program compliance, and the planning and implementation of youth-led community events.

Major Duties and Responsibilities

**Youth Recruitment, Employment & Retention**

* Recruit, screen, and facilitate the hiring of 15 youth from the Brighton Park community.
* Maintain consistent communication with youth to support recruitment, engagement, and retention throughout the program.
* Provide ongoing mentorship, coaching, guidance, and advocacy to assigned youth participants.
* Develop and maintain positive relationships with youth, community partners, and partner site leads.
* Communicate program expectations, policies, procedures, and employment requirements to all participants.
* Follow up with youth who demonstrate inconsistent attendance or disengagement to address barriers and encourage continued participation.

**Employability Skills Training and Career Development**

* Facilitates individual and group-based workshops designed to strengthen participants' employment readiness and professional development.
* Provides training in workplace behaviors, communication, professionalism, financial literacy, digital literacy, career exploration, and other essential employability skills.
* Registers youth for upcoming job readiness workshops, training opportunities, and career development activities.
* Facilitates employability skills training that prepares youth for successful entry into the workforce and long-term career advancement.

**Community Events & Safe Space Engagement**

* Collaborate with program youth to plan, coordinate, and implement nine (9) community events throughout the program year, in accordance with the funder's established timeline.
* Ensure all nine events take place within the Brighton Park community and provide safe, welcoming, and engaging spaces for youth and community members.
* Develop events that offer fun, recreational, and educational activities while connecting attendees to valuable community resources and services.
* Coordinate event logistics, including food and beverage arrangements, giveaways, community resources, vendors, supplies, and activities.
* Encourage youth leadership and active participation in the planning, coordination, and implementation of each event.
* Ensure participant surveys are distributed and completed by youth attendees to collect feedback, measure engagement, and document program outcomes.
* Monitor survey completion and maintain accurate documentation to ensure all funder-required event deliverables and reporting requirements are met.
* Ensure each event aligns with program objectives, funder expectations, and the overall goal of creating safe spaces and strengthening community engagement.
* Identify, recruit, and engage community-based organizations, service providers, and local partners to participate in community kickback events.
* Coordinate with community partners to secure resource tables and informational materials that connect youth and community members to valuable resources, services, and support.
* Maintain positive relationships with community partners to encourage ongoing collaboration and participation in program events.
* Ensure participating partners provide relevant resources and information that address the needs and interests of youth and families in the Brighton Park community.

**Payroll, Administrative Responsibilities, and Reporting**

* Coordinate and process payroll for the 15 youth participants.
* Track, review, manage, and verify the accuracy of youth timesheets prior to payroll approval.
* Enter and maintain accurate youth attendance and timesheet records in the Cityspan system.
* Monitor the completion and submission of all required youth enrollment, employment, and program documentation.
* Ensure youth are registered and connected to the My CHI My Future (MCMF) platform.
